blocks.text: Why you need to edit out filler words

Filler words like ums and ahs break the rhythm of your conversation. While some natural speech is fine, too many distract your listeners. High-quality shows maintain a professional pace by removing these interruptions. This makes your content easier to follow and increases listener retention.
The true cost of manual audio editing

Editing is the largest time sink for most podcast producers. You likely spend 2 to 5 hours for every single hour of finished audio. If you have a weekly show, this can consume most of your production time. This leaves little room for show strategy, guest research, or marketing. When you perform this work manually, you face constant decision fatigue. You must decide if every single pause or filler word is worth cutting. This adds thousands of micro-decisions to your workday.
Common causes of long editing sessions

items: Poor recording environments that require extensive noise removal.
Lack of a standardized template in your DAW.
Attempting to fix every single breath or minor imperfection.
High audience expectations for polished, professional audio.

blocks.text: Fixes anyone can use for faster editing

You do not need expensive hardware to speed up your process. Start by recording in a room with soft surfaces to kill echo. Use a microphone with a pop filter to reduce plosives. These simple steps mean you spend less time in post-production fixing audio quality. Create a master template in your DAW. This template should include your intro, outro, and standard compression settings. You will save time by not setting these up for every new episode.

faq.question: How can I edit out filler words faster?
faq.answer: Switch to transcript-based editing tools. These allow you to edit audio by deleting text directly in a document interface.

faq.question: Is it worth paying someone to edit my podcast?
faq.answer: If your editing time prevents you from growing your show, it is often worth the cost. Professional editors charge between $150 and $350 per episode.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit audio files for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It guides you to the right tools and helps you find settings within your apps.
